long_biography.plain_text:
Saxo Bank grew from a phone-and-fax brokerage into an early online-investing platform under Kim Fournais. After deciding academic study did not suit him, the Danish founder learned stockbroking and saw an industry with opaque prices and poor client service. He made better technology and wider market access the business's organising idea.

Fournais bought Vejrø, a Danish island that he developed around regenerative agriculture, hospitality and independent energy, water and heat systems. A licensed commercial pilot, he flew himself between European offices while leading the bank. The island now combines a resort, restaurants, farming and a marina with its own microgrid.

uncertainties.detail: Forbes was searched first using exact-name, company, nationality, billionaire and profile combinations. Forbes has an attributable Saxo article but no dedicated Kim Fournais person profile. Identity is nevertheless resolved at very high confidence through official Saxo leadership and regulatory records plus multiple direct interviews; the source-record vessel is unnecessary and excluded.

The source record's day and year are correct, but its January month conflicts with Saxo's regulatory annual report and prospectus, both of which give 30 June 1966. June is proposed as a correction. Copenhagen and Denmark are proposed from a direct profile corroborated by the regulatory identity. Current official and direct March and July 2026 material supports correcting mortality from Unknown to Alive.

The March 2026 majority transaction left Fournais with approximately 28 percent of Saxo through Fournais Holding, and a July release announced the acquisition of his remaining 28.69 percent stake subject to regulatory approval. Saxo's current investor-relations page now records 100 percent ownership by J. Safra Sarasin and Fournais as chairman. The terms and reinvestment of his proceeds are private, so Finance & Investments rests on his realised Saxo wealth and continuing sector role rather than a claimed current shareholding.

Self-made — independent start is based on positive evidence: a non-business public-sector professional family, Fournais' departure from formal study, his learned stockbroking skill, jointly assembled modest seed capital, and a launch without clients or an established brand. The classification does not claim poverty or exclude ordinary family support.

The official Saxo leadership page is proposed as Company Website because it directly identifies Fournais as founder and chairman. Searches of LinkedIn, Instagram, Facebook, X, YouTube, TikTok, Wikipedia and personal websites did not produce an identity-secure personal account. Corporate Saxo social posts and Wikidata are evidence leads, not proposed personal profiles.

Fintech is the minimum useful industry tag and the overlapping broader Banking tag is omitted. Resort operations captures two decades of owner-led Vejrø development and the current hospitality platform. Art collector reflects Fournais' sustained direction of the 595-work corporate collection while explicitly not claiming personal title to every work. Pilot is not assigned because commercial flying is character detail rather than a defining occupation, and Engineer is not assigned because the sources establish study rather than a defining engineering practice.

The short biography uses family background, initial capital and the chief-executive-to-chairman transition. The long biography independently develops the service problem, technology model, flying and Vejrø project. Both exclude the source-record vessel, current valuation, personal wealth estimates and the pending stake-sale mechanics.
